Hi everyone! Apologies for posting about this a bit late. Since I am still relatively new to this part of mathlib, I wanted to spend some time exploring the API and experimenting on my own before asking for feedback.

I am currently working on #37940 formalizing the category of local algebras with a fixed residue field (as a foundation for formal deformation theory). From the very beginning, I have been looking at CommAlgCat and AlgCat as reference points for my design.

However, I noticed a difference in how the morphisms are handled. For categories like CommAlgCat or AlgCat, the design wraps an already existing bundled homomorphism (like AlgHom) inside a new Hom structure.

My question is about the best practice here: in my case, can I just use the bundled homomorphism (local algebra homomorphisms compatible with residue maps) directly as the morphisms in the category, or is there a strong structural reason to wrap it in a new Hom structure?

Any advice or pointers to similar design choices in mathlib would be greatly appreciated!

Hi Bingyu!

I don't know enough about deformation theory to say if the definitions/theorems you wrote are correct, but I left some a few comments about general style across your code. I hope it is helpful for cleaning up the code at least.

Bingyu Xia said:

My question is about the best practice here: in my case, can I just use the bundled homomorphism (local algebra homomorphisms compatible with residue maps) directly as the morphisms in the category, or is there a strong structural reason to wrap it in a new Hom structure?

I am not really sure. I would love to get some advice on this too! My guess would be that it is generally better to define a "bundled morphism" structure separately--that way you can prove things directly about the morphism type rather than always needing to unwrap it.

Bingyu Xia said:

Any advice or pointers to similar design choices in mathlib would be greatly appreciated!

I think one piece of advice would be to shorten the PR length... 1500 lines and 5 new files is a little much for most ppl to review in one sitting.

A few other thoughts about the PR overall:

  • I think your proofs could be more refined. You have too many proofs that are 50+ lines long with heavy simp, rw, and have use. This usually indicates missing API. I tagged them with "golf proof".
  • You need to work on the instance chain. Many of your files are overly-reliant on letI, haveI and especially abbrev. This is a performance concern.
  • You also introduce new set_option backwards which is only supposed to be used for backwards compatibility, not for new code.
You might want to look at the Deformations folder in the FLT repo where we have a lot of the foundations is deformation theory. It was written by @Andrew Yang .

@Jack McCarthy Thank you for taking the time to review my PR and for the helpful suggestions! I will think carefully about the points you raised.

Regarding the heavy use of letI and haveI for the instance chain, part of this is because of the IsLocalHom condition. I was trying to avoid using it as a global instance. Another thing that led to several haveIs in my code is the lack of a global instance like: [IsLocalRing A] [Nontrivial (A ⧸ I)] : IsLocalRing (A ⧸ I). But I suspected there might be a specific structural or performance reason why such a simple fact isn't already a global instance in mathlib.

I will also look into the other issues you mentioned (like golfing the proofs). Thanks again!

I second the advice given above to split it: +1500 is way too long, and you’ll have a much better time finding reviewers if you write a series of PRs with a much smaller diff. From a very quick look I see that you are adding several files with new defs/math content in the PR: splitting each file as its own PR could be a starting point to shorten things.
The "big PR" with the full diff is still useful as a draft for reviewers if they want a quick look at how things in the smaller PRs fit together.

(now at a computer): take a look at https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/tree/main/FLT/Deformations

For example in https://github.com/ImperialCollegeLondon/FLT/blob/main/FLT/Deformations/Categories.lean you can see Andrew's definition of the category of local proartinian algebras over 𝓞 (a topological local ring with residue field 𝕜) with fixed residue field 𝕜.

I should say that this was written before we discovered that every compact Hausdorff local ring was proArtinian and we might well end up moving to compact Hausdorff local rings with a fixed residue field in later iterations.
